blocks.h: Section A: modern drama, An Inspector Calls

questions.q: EITHER (1) How does Priestley present Sheila as a character who changes? OR (2) How does Priestley use the Inspector to challenge the Birlings? You must refer to the context of the play.
questions.a: AO1 (15) and AO2 (15). Indicative content (1): Sheila's privileged opening ('pleased with life'); immediate guilt over Eva in Act 1; her growing insight ('he's giving us the rope'); her refusal to pretend in Act 3; Priestley's hope in the younger generation. (2): the Inspector's control of pace and the 'one line of enquiry'; the photograph; his final speech ('We are members of one body'); dramatic irony and the play's structure.

questions.q: EITHER (3) How does Shakespeare present ambition in Macbeth? OR (4) How does Shakespeare present the relationship between Macbeth and Lady Macbeth? You must refer to the context of the play.
questions.a: AO1 (10), AO2 (10), AO4 (10). Indicative content (3): 'vaulting ambition' (1.7); the witches' prophecies; Lady Macbeth's 'unsex me here' (1.5); guilt and tyranny; the Divine Right of Kings and the Jacobean view of regicide. (4): Lady Macbeth's early dominance and challenges to his manhood; the shift after Duncan's murder; isolation ('Be innocent of the knowledge'); the sleepwalking scene (5.1); 'She should have died hereafter'.
